column1: # What the KDE configuration in config/ NAMES but cannot contain.
# Nothing here is stored in this repo — it is fetched on the machine that
# needs it. The icon set alone is 129 MB across 15,706 files; the rest is
# small, but keeping the whole set on one route is worth more than saving a
# few megabytes on some of it.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   source   store | git | aur
#   ref      KDE Store content id  |  git URL  |  package name
#   pattern  store: ERE matched against the download file names, last match
#            wins (so a version bump upstream still resolves).
#            git: the sub-directory holding metadata.json, "." for the root.
#   method   tar:<dir under ~/.local/share>  |  kpackage:<KPackage type>
#   target   path under ~/.local/share that exists once it is installed;
#            this is what makes the script skip work already done.
# Why the look-and-feel and Plasma style are unpacked with tar rather than
# installed with kpackagetool6, which is the obvious tool and was how they were
# installed here by hand in the first place:
#   kpackagetool6 -t Plasma/LookAndFeel -i Beauty-Color-Global-6.tar.gz
# resolves the global theme's dependencies through KNewStuff and downloads them
# — measured 2026-09-24 into an empty home: 89,470 files, 817 MB of icon themes,
# five of them, none of which is the Slot-Beauty-Dark-Icons-V-3 the config
# actually selects, plus both colour schemes, both wallpapers and the Aurorae
# theme. Unpacking the same archive with tar produces 9 files and nothing else.
# So the tar route is not a simplification, it is the difference between
# fetching ~140 MB that is used and ~960 MB that mostly is not. It also explains
# the five unused icon sets sitting in this machine's own ~/.local/share/icons:
# nobody chose them.
# The .plasmoid and applet entries below stay on kpackagetool6 — a .plasmoid is
# a zip, tar cannot open it, and applets pull nothing in.
# Store ids come from ~/.local/share/kde-store-installs.md, written by hand
# on 2026-09-23 while these were installed one at a time. Without that file
# this list could not have been reconstructed — the Store has no "what did I
# install" view.
